subject: Kestrel.ai — inference routing, SDK & auth checklist
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@kestrel.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@kestrel.ai>
Date: 2026-07-14 15:12 -0700
Subject: Kestrel post-demo: SDK/auth checklist + Qs on routing
Attachments: kestrel_security_questionnaire.pdf (pdf, 420KB)

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the demo earlier — Raj and I found the routing controls and the latency/cost tradeoff examples really helpful. A few follow-ups from our side so we can scope the POC: 

1) SDK & auth: we prefer a non-interactive service account flow (server-to-server). Is there a recommended pattern for short-lived credentials (mTLS vs OAuth2 with rotating keys)? We also need an example Node or Python SDK snippet that shows: init, model selection, structured output (tool-calling), and embeddings call.

2) Routing/policy: primary goal is 99th percentile latency < 180ms for chat features. Secondary is to cap inference cost per request to $0.06. Would like recommended policy examples: latency-first route + cost-aware fallback chain. Also region controls — we want US customers served from us-west primarily, with EU failover.

3) Security/compliance: attached questionnaire; SOC2 items and logging/audit evidence requested (particularly data retention and KMS integration).

Can you send a short post-call checklist and proposed next steps so our infra team can evaluate?

Thanks,
Samira
Head of AI, Kestrel.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@kestrel.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@kestrel.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-14 17:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Kestrel post-demo: SDK/auth checklist + Qs on routing

Samira — great meeting, thanks to you and Raj. Below is a concise post-call recap and an initial checklist your infra team can use. I’ll also loop in engineering for a short workshop.

Quick recap (actionable items):
- Auth: We support both short-lived OAuth2 tokens (recommended for server-to-server with rotation via our token service) and mTLS for strict environments. For your use case (service account with automated rotation) we recommend OAuth2 + KMS-wrapped refresh tokens.
- SDKs: Python and Node SDKs available. I attached an internal snippet below and will send a small sample repo on Drive.
- Routing/policy: propose a two-tier policy: 
  * Primary: latency-first route — route to hosted GPU pool (gpus: A10x / A100) when predicted latency < 140ms.
  * Fallback: quantized L2 70B int8 on Dedicated pool or our CPU-optimized embeddings endpoint when cost cap exceeded.
  * Cost throttle: per-request budget check (configurable) — if estimated cost > $0.06, auto-fallback to lower-cost model or cached prefix.
- Region routing: default us-west for US traffic; eu-west as automatic regional failover. We can pin sessions to region or include per-request region hints.
- Structured output/tool-calling: we recommend using function-calling schema in SDK v2.1 — infer+tool-call pipeline sample included.
- Embeddings/reranker: recommend separate embeddings endpoint for candidate generation + a lightweight reranker (distil model) to keep latency low.

Next steps / ownership:
1) Technical workshop (90 min) — workshop to include SDK auth walkthrough, sample routing policy creation, and a live fallback demo. Proposed slots: Thu 7/16 10:00 PT or Fri 7/17 13:00 PT. 
2) We will provide: sample repo (Python/Node), example routing policy JSON, SOW draft, SOC2 evidence pointers.
3) Kestrel to return: completed security questionnaire, preferred auth pattern, initial list of routes/regions to test.

Embedded SDK snippet (Node):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, region: 'us-west' });

// structured output (function / tool call)
const res = await client.chat.create({
  model: 'redwood-chat-2',
  messages: [{role: 'user', content: 'Summarize flight logs.'}],
  functions: [{name: 'get_flight_log', parameters: {type: 'object'}}],
  routingHints: {policyId: 'kstl-latency-first'}
});

Attachments: (I will upload the sample repo link after this message)

I'll put Ben and Monica on point for the workshop and sample code.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@kestrel.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-15 09:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Kestrel post-demo: SDK/auth checklist + Qs on routing

Samira — quick auth implementation notes from infra/SDK side: 

- For service accounts we provide a short-lived token endpoint (recommended). Flow: service account private key (stored in your KMS) -> request short-lived JWT from our auth service -> exchange for bearer token (15m TTL). We can optionally sign tokens with customer KMS if you need complete key separation.
- mTLS: supported on Private deployments — we can provide cert rotation guidance.
- SDK sample (Python) — pseudo snippet: 
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(token_endpoint=os.environ['RW_TOKEN_ENDPOINT'])
# pass routing policy hint
resp = client.chat.create(model='redwood-chat-2', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'...'}], routing_hints={'policy':'kstl-latency-first'})

Attaching proposed routing policy for the POC as text in the workshop. I’ll also include a cost-estimator script that plugs into your CI to simulate per-request cost before hitting prod.

—Ben
Principal SDK Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@kestrel.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Kestrel post-demo: SDK/auth checklist + Qs on routing

Thanks Vivek/Ben. A couple of procurement/security items before the workshop: 

- Can you send the SOW draft and an expected pricing band for the POC (1 month, expected 5M tokens, embedding volume ~50k vectors)? Procurement needs a ballpark for approvals.
- On fallback chains: we need an explicit example showing behavior when a region is under load — e.g., if us-west latency breaches 180ms, how are requests routed (eu-west? lower-cost model? cached responses?). Please include a decision tree and testing checklist.
- SOC2 evidence: which artifacts can you provide immediately (audit logs, retention policy, KMS config examples)? The questionnaire is in the first message.

Would prefer the workshop on Thu 7/16 10:00 PT. Please attach the SOW and a Drive link with code before then.

—Raj
VP Product, Kestrel.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@kestrel.ai>, Samira Khan <samira@kestrel.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-16 10:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Kestrel post-demo: SDK/auth checklist + Qs on routing
Attachments: redwood_sow-draft.docx (docx, 38KB); kestrel_integration_diagram.png (png, 210KB)

Raj/Samira — thanks. Confirming workshop Thu 7/16 10:00 PT. Attached: SOW draft and a high-level integration diagram. Also uploaded sample repo and routing policy templates to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/kestrel-integration

Quick answers inline: 
- SOW / pricing: draft attached. For the POC (1 month, 5M tokens + 50k embeddings) estimate: hosted API band $6k–$9k depending on model selection (we included a conservative and aggressive option in the SOW). Final pricing will be in the signed SOW.
- Fallback decision tree (summary):
  1) Pre-check per-request: estimate latency using model profiling + prefix cache. If estimated_p95 < 140ms -> route to primary hosted GPU pool (us-west).
  2) If runtime monitoring shows p95 > 180ms OR error rate > 0.5% -> trigger failover window: route to eu-west regional pool for geo-eligible requests.
  3) If cost estimate for primary model > per-request budget ($0.06) -> fallback to quantized variant on Dedicated (L2-70B-int8) or cached response.
  4) Last-resort: return a short system message + best-effort summary (graceful degradation) and log the incident for post-mortem.

We will demo the decision tree and simulated region failover during the workshop. For SOC2 artifacts: we can provide audit log exports (redacted), KMS integration checklist, and our PCA attestation summary. The detailed questionnaire responses will follow by EOD.

Action items assigned:
- Redwood: upload sample repo + routing policy examples (Ben) — DONE on Drive.
- Kestrel: return completed security questionnaire and preferred auth method (Samira).
- Both: confirm any additional data residency constraints before the workshop.

DocuSign link for SOW will be sent after your internal review: https://www.docusign.net/link/to/sow/98765

See you Thu 10:00 PT — calendar invite sent.

Best,
Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
